governanceNotes: D1 batch 68 (2026-09-26): identity deferred (SHARED-SUBSTRATE with the retention/obstruction/neurogenic families plus zero condition-specific outcome quantification). Overflow incontinence is the leakage manifestation of chronic urinary retention with high post-void residual, and the located evidence supports no outgoing catalog edge: (i) cystitis from urinary stasis - mechanistically plausible but the quantified urinary-tract-infection evidence sits in spinal-cord-injury neurogenic-bladder and catheter-management populations whose cord-syndrome and retention windows own their evidence (ME-29), and no overflow-phenotype-specific infection incidence was located; (ii) hydronephrosis from back-pressure - the obstructive-uropathy and retention literature quantifies upper-tract damage in obstruction states where the obstruction (meatal-stenosis, prostate disease, neuropathy) is the causal agent and its own windows carry the pathway (the meatal-stenosis hydronephrosis window is the registered back-pressure precedent); (iii) chronic kidney disease - same shared-driver structure; (iv) the only located generic complication framing is StatPearls-class narrative (postoperative urinary retention review, PMID 31751034), below the authoring standard and already flagged in the weak-citation backlog class. Reopening conditions: (a) a cohort quantifying urinary-tract-infection, hydronephrosis, or renal-outcome incidence in chronic urinary retention/overflow populations with post-void residual documentation and obstruction/neuropathy adjustment; or (b) a governance decision treating overflow incontinence as a manifestation facet of the urinary-frequency-retention identity rather than a standalone mapping source.
